title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
description: The Key to Theosophy by H. P. Blavatsky (London: Theosophical Publishing Company, 1889), 'being a clear exposition, in the form of question and answer, of the ethics, science and philosophy for the study of which the Theosophical Society has been founded'. Written for general readers, it is the most accessible of Blavatsky's major works. In a dialogue between an 'Enquirer' and a 'Theosophist', it explains what Theosophy is and is not, the aims of the Theosophical Society (universal brotherhood, comparative study of religion, philosophy and science, and investigation of the unexplained laws of nature and latent human powers), the difference between Theosophy and Spiritualism, the septenary nature of the human being, the states of the soul after death (Kama-loka and Devachan), reincarnation and karma, the nature of the Masters or Mahatmas, and practical ethics. It includes a glossary of Sanskrit and esoteric terms.
